## What is publicly documented

::: {.case-evidence}
Karuk public materials describe cultural-fire practitioner support. Good Fire II addresses barriers to beneficial fire; a published California agreement offers an example of enabling conditions.
:::

Sources: [Karuk Tribe: Eco-Culture Revitalization](https://www.karuk.us/departments/natural-resources-dnr/eco-culture-revitalization); [Karuk Tribe: Good Fire II](https://www.karuk.us/posts/good-fire-2-report-officially-released); [Karuk Tribe: California–Karuk cultural burning agreement](https://www.karuk.us/posts/california-partners-with-karuk-tribe-on-groundbreaking-cultural-burning-agreement). Reviewed October 14, 2026.

## Relationship status

Potential learning relationship; no invitation or agreement is implied.

## A proposed question to discuss

Which lessons about authority, practitioner support and sustained implementation might inform discussions elsewhere?

This question was drafted for the prototype; it is not attributed to the Nation, organization or practitioners.

## A possible learning contribution

Examine enabling institutions alongside ecological observations.

## What remains context-specific

Karuk practices and California-specific arrangements are not transferable prescriptions for other Nations or states.
